preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 100) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 100 for n in (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line contains an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 100) representing the number of teams in a test case.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.split()) == sum(n * (n - 1) // 2 for n in (int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n(n-1)/2 integers per test case, representing the results of all games in the specified order.

postconditions.expression: all(-1 <= int(result) <= 1 for result in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: Each game result is either -1 (loss for team x), 0 (tie), or 1 (win for team x).

postconditions.expression: all(calculate_total_score(n, results) == calculate_total_score(n, results)[0] for n, results in zip((int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]), split_output_by_test_cases(stdout)))
postconditions.description: For each test case, all teams have the same total score, where calculate_total_score(n, results) returns a list of scores for each team.

postconditions.expression: all(minimize_ties(n, results) for n, results in zip((int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]), split_output_by_test_cases(stdout)))
postconditions.description: The number of ties in the output is minimized for each test case, where minimize_ties(n, results) checks if the number of 0s in results is the smallest possible.
